key_insight: PRISM is a retrieval-augmented multimodal model that fuses structured EHR data, ECG history, and cohort memory to improve clinical prognosis prediction.
clinical_relevance: It may help forecast outcomes such as diagnosis, deterioration, ICU admission, and mortality by integrating multiple evidence streams rather than relying on a single data source.
method: Encodes per-feature numerical EHR data and recency-weighted longitudinal ECG signals.
Retrieves similar cohort information in embedding space using a population memory bank without exposing individual records in the prompt.
Combines heterogeneous evidence with frozen encoders for prognosis prediction and external adaptation.
evidence_signal: On the MDS-ED benchmark, PRISM reported AUROCs of 86.2% for diagnosis, 93.1% for deterioration, 91.8% for ICU admission, and 92.8% for mortality, with the strongest external cohort result reaching 0.8611 AUROC after fine-tuning.
watch_item: Performance comparisons may be sensitive to the 96-hour pre-arrival window and benchmark-specific inputs, so real-world generalization and implementation should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Language Model with Heterogeneous Evidence Integration for Clinical Prognosis
